newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex says 100,000 bbl gasoline lost in fire.
newsitem.headline: Pemex says 100,000 bbl gasoline lost in fire.

text.p: The explosion and fire at a Pemex storage and distribution depot in northern Mexico City has burned off about 100,000 barrels of gasoline and caused a loss of about 40 million pesos ($5.05 million), Pemex Director General Adrian Lajous said Tuesday.
"We expect it (the fire) to be extinguished in the next few hours," Lajous, chief of the state-owned monopoly, told the Televisa television network in an interview.
"It is still early for a precise cost of the accident," he added. "A preliminary estimate puts it in the order of 40 million pesos."
That estimate includes lost fuel and repair costs, he said.

Lajous said a gasoline leak during a valve repair on a "D-8" storage tank caused the explosion at the Valley of Mexico North Terminal. But he would provide no further details pending an investigation. He said 13 Pemex workers and two firefighters were injured, four of them gravely.

Lajous called it the third major accident in the past 20 months and said this incident and the overall safety of Pemex installations would be investigated thoroughly by several bodies including a specially appointed commission.
"Pemex is obligated to offer a precise and punctual explanation regarding what happened at the terminal," Lajous said. "I personally assume this obligation.
"Public opinion demands and deserves a more ample and general explanation regarding the safety conditions of installations in the petroleum industry," he added.

Lajous said the approximate 100,000 barrels burned is equal to slightly less than the gasoline consumed in one day by the 18 million people in the greater Mexico City area known as the Valley of Mexico.
But he said there would be no shortage of fuel because Pemex "has sufficient inventories in other terminals in refineries that supply the whole region."
Nearly all of the fuel burned was the Magna and Nova brands gasoline used for automobiles, but a small amount of diesel and other fuel in the process of being refined also was lost, Lajous said.
